carried_run_shard_schedule: writer-shared round-robin without reuse before 64 shards
comparison_contract: Every producer pipelines four durable append tickets through the public GroupCommitWriter API and retains stable affinity to one worker lane, so its tickets form groups. Eight independent lanes publish concurrently through the shared collection-WAL coordination protocol, removing process-local head-of-line blocking across producers without weakening acknowledgement semantics. A successful group visibility CAS may atomically install exactly one fresh GC-protecting successor reservation in the same checked frontier HEAD; the lane reuses it for the next group without a reservation GET+PUT, stops after four same-shard commits, then returns to ordinary random-shard admission. No batch is pre-reserved. Capacity, contention, expiry, ambiguous CAS recovery, and graceful shutdown drop or cancel the successor without weakening the final visibility authority. Public BorsukIndex mutation APIs retain ordinary per-transaction admission. The process-shared last-write-wins allocator observes the durable counter once per group but CAS-reserves a disjoint 4096-generation range only when stale or exhausted; public BorsukIndex::put retains per-call durable allocation, and sequential cross-API ordering is a required test. Per-operation latency runs from submission through durable receipt. Every cell uses the same source archive, instance type, dimensions, group bounds, raw-sample schema, and full inserted-vector point-visibility check. Twenty preregistered inserted vectors provide known exact top-1 ground truth and are queried through the bounded production SrhtPqScan path; every query must return its exact ID with recall@1 1.0 and read p95 below 200 ms. A writer-count/repetition cohort is identical across the paired 2K and 16K cell counts and deliberately distinct from other writer counts to prevent equal-vector ID ties in the persistent index. Cell count and concurrent producer count are the only matrix factors. Each completed cell must also have write p95 below 200 ms and throughput at least 5 records/s per configured writer (5, 40, and 160 records/s); a miss writes gate-specific markers and terminates the campaign before later cells. The 2K index and matrix complete before constructing the 16K index, so a 2K gate failure cannot waste the 16K bootstrap. Five repetitions are mandatory; no incomplete CSV is eligible for inspection.
